report.summary: 4 surviving findings: high-severity trace_id mismatch and offload_runner exception handling need inspection; medium-severity batch size validation and mutable env isolation need grep/defensive changes. Steps reference only paths from findings.
risks: If offload_runner raises exceptions, cascading failures in _recording_runner and _default_attempt are unhandled.
If trace_id is absent from task shape, intents may be misattributed across trace contexts.
No cross-module batch size validation could cause silent timeouts or overflows.
Mutable dict from council_env could be accidentally mutated, affecting subprocess environments.
todos: Inspect daedalus/eval/tasks.py for trace_id field in TASKS list.
Inspect all call sites of record_intent to verify explicit trace_id passing.
Inspect offload_runner implementation for possible exceptions.
Grep for 'batch' and 'limit' in codebase to confirm absence of cross-module validation.
Grep for 'council_env' callers to verify none mutate the returned dict.

items.title: Inspect trace_id presence in eval tasks and record_intent call sites
items.why_now: Without confirming trace_id is explicit, intents may be misattributed in eval, corrupting provenance.

steps.do: Open daedalus/eval/tasks.py and check if the TASKS list includes a trace_id field in each task shape.
steps.verified_by: Manual inspection: grep for 'trace_id' in daedalus/eval/tasks.py

steps.do: Grep for all calls to record_intent in the codebase and verify each passes trace_id explicitly.
steps.verified_by: grep -rn 'record_intent' daedalus/ -- list each call and confirm trace_id argument

items.assumption: We assume the TASKS list is defined in daedalus/eval/tasks.py and record_intent is defined in daedalus/spine/ledger.py.

items.title: Inspect offload_runner for exception safety and add handling if needed
items.why_now: If offload_runner can raise, _recording_runner and _default_attempt will crash without recovery.

steps.do: Find the definition of offload_runner (likely in daedalus/eval/ or daedalus/kairos/) and inspect its implementation for possible exceptions.
steps.verified_by: grep -rn 'def offload_runner' daedalus/ -- then review the file

steps.do: Check if run_attempt (likely in daedalus/spine/attempt.py) catches exceptions from offload_runner.
steps.verified_by: Manual inspection of daedalus/spine/attempt.py for try/except around offload_runner call

items.assumption: We assume offload_runner is defined somewhere in daedalus/eval/ or daedalus/kairos/; exact path unknown.

items.title: Add cross-module batch size validation
items.why_now: Without validation, a large batch from one module can cause timeout/overflow in another without feedback.

steps.do: Search for any existing cross-module batch size validation by grepping for 'batch' and 'limit'.
steps.verified_by: grep -rn -E 'batch|limit' daedalus/ -- if no cross-module validation found, claim holds

steps.do: Add a shared batch size limit constant and validate input size before processing in modules that consume batches.
steps.verified_by: Write a test that passes a batch exceeding the limit and asserts graceful rejection

items.assumption: We assume batch-consuming modules exist (e.g., projection worker, wiki link processor) but exact files unknown.

items.title: Protect council_env return value from mutation
items.why_now: The docstring guarantee is not enforced; a future caller could mutate the dict and affect subprocess environments.

steps.do: Grep for all callers of council_env to verify none mutate the result.
steps.verified_by: grep -rn 'council_env' daedalus/ -- then inspect each caller's code for mutations

steps.do: Change council_env to return a read-only view (e.g., types.MappingProxyType) to enforce the docstring guarantee.

items.assumption: We assume council_env is defined in daedalus/council/session.py and tests exist.
